Each pair of distinct circles meets in at most 2 points. Four circles form C(4,2) = 6 pairs, so there are at most 6 × 2 = 12 intersection points. This bound is achievable: take four congruent circles with centers spread out so that every pair overlaps, with no three circles sharing a point. That gives exactly 12 distinct points.

The proposed solution's count of 14 is impossible. Its construction also fails on its own terms. Two distinct circles share at most 2 points, so a third circle through A and B cannot meet the first two circles anywhere else. The solution also counts some points twice.

The correct answer is 12.
